works.title: Gated Linear Attention Transformers with Hardware-Efficient Training
works.note: Shows data-dependent gating makes linear attention competitive with softmax attention and Mamba at 340M/1.3B scale trained on 15B/100B tokens, i.e. gates help at convergence, though its gate modulates the recurrent state rather than the block output.

works.title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
works.note: Shows gating combined with the delta rule consistently surpasses plain DeltaNet and Mamba2 across language-modeling and retrieval benchmarks at full training, directly contradicting the finding's 30-epoch reversal where the gated DeltaNet ends 1.7 PPL worse.

works.title: Gated Slot Attention for Efficient Linear-Time Sequence Modeling
works.note: Shows adding a GLA-inspired gating mechanism to a linear-attention memory improves language modeling by a large margin over the ungated ABC baseline, arguing gates help final quality.

works.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
works.note: Identifies input-dependent selective gates as the key mechanism that lets SSMs match Transformers on language at convergence, contradicting convergence-time harm from input-dependent gating.

works.title: GLU Variants Improve Transformer
works.note: Shows sigmoid-style multiplicative gating (SwiGLU etc.) improves final quality over ReLU/GELU FFNs at matched parameter counts in fully trained T5 models, though it tests FFN gating rather than attention-output gating.

works.title: Language Modeling with Gated Convolutional Networks
works.note: Shows gated linear units reach higher accuracy and converge faster than LSTM-style gating thanks to a gradient path without downscaling, direct evidence that multiplicative gating accelerates early training as in the finding.

works.title: Efficient Global Neural Architecture Search
works.note: Measures Spearman rank correlation of only ~0.65 between 1-epoch and 50-epoch validation accuracy across 240 sampled architectures, quantifying that short-training rankings mis-rank candidates exactly as the finding concludes.

works.title: NAS evaluation is frustratingly hard
works.note: Shows architecture and method rankings shift with training budgets and comparison protocols, so conclusions drawn at low budgets are unreliable and need matching-budget controls.

works.title: Neural Architecture Search: A Survey
works.note: Documents that low-fidelity performance estimates (shorter training, smaller data) bias evaluation and that relative rankings can change dramatically when the fidelity gap to full evaluation is large, motivating gradual fidelity increases.

works.title: Understanding and Robustifying Differentiable Architecture Search
works.note: Shows low search-phase validation loss can coincide with sharply curved minima and poor final test performance, and that regularization restores generalization, an early-win/late-loss pattern matching the gate's overfitting.

works.title: Learning Transferable Architectures for Scalable Image Recognition
works.note: Establishes the proxy-search paradigm (fewer epochs, smaller data) whose transferred NASNet cells still achieved state of the art, showing short-fidelity search can work even though rankings are not generally preserved.

works.title: SpikeGPT: Generative Pre-trained Language Model with Spiking Neural Networks
works.note: Shows RWKV-style gated recurrence in a directly trained spiking language model stays competitive with non-spiking baselines, evidence gating is viable in SNN LMs, but it reports no epoch-wise or DeltaNet comparison.

output.summary: Gate benefits at convergence are well attested in non-spiking linear attention (GLA, Gated DeltaNet, GSA, Mamba, GLU variants), so the 30-epoch reversal is unexpected against that literature. But gated units are also known to converge faster (Dauphin), and the NAS literature firmly documents short-training rankings diverging from full-training rankings (Spearman ~0.65 at 1 epoch; Zela; Elsken; Yang). The crossover in a spiking model, with training PPL staying lower, is a novel small-scale confirmation that 2-epoch evolutionary proxies reward fast early learners. Overall the conclusion is expected; the specific spiking-DeltaNet crossover point is the new evidence, and multi-fidelity confirmation is the right remedy.
